chapters.record: OUT-001 Patients can book, move or cancel an appointment themselves at any time of day
chapters.draft: Patients can book, move, or cancel their appointments themselves through the online service at any time of day, ensuring convenient access to appointment management independently of clinic hours.

chapters.record: QD-001 Quality: Book an appointment at any time through the online service
chapters.draft: The system must enable patients to book an appointment at any time through the online service, supporting continuous access without temporal restrictions, as described in REQ-001 acceptance criteria.

chapters.record: ADR-001 How should the design respect CON-001: Patient personal data must be handled in line with the health data regulation that applies where the clinic operates?
chapters.draft: The chosen design respects CON-001 by ensuring that patient personal data is managed fully within the health data regulation applicable to the clinic's location. Two alternatives were considered: keeping all data and operations within a single owned boundary to maintain transaction integrity and simpler ownership, or separating the governed work into an independent boundary to enable isolated change and failure handling. This rationale explains the trade-offs between simpler control and ownership versus increased modularity and isolation, guiding how the design aligns with regulations while addressing quality drivers such as data integrity.
Enables patients to book appointments anytime through the online service, providing a self-service scheduling capability outside the clinical records and prescription systems.

Owns the Appointment scheduling service, enabling patients to book appointments online at any time. Does not handle clinical records, prescriptions, phone bookings, reminders, or confirmation of reminders, which are outside its scope.

chapters.record: TC-001 Compute for Appointment scheduling service
chapters.draft: Provide compute resources to enable the APP-001 Appointment scheduling service to operate its owned application logic and data, ensuring patients can book appointments at any time via the online service.

chapters.record: TR-001 Compute for Appointment scheduling service implementation
chapters.draft: The operation, monitoring, and support responsibilities for this compute implementation are currently unassigned and unresolved, as no details are specified in the design brief or upstream records. This remains an open question requiring definition before progressing.

The contract currently does not specify a failure policy; this remains an open question without explicit guidance on handling failures or uncertain outcomes when delivering appointment booking responses.

The Appointment scheduling service is ready to serve when its compute capability (Compute for Appointment scheduling service) responds and is operational, confirming that the required single replica is active and ready within its trust boundary zone.

chapters.record: SDD Sol live check · reference — Solution Design
chapters.draft: This design enables patients to book, move, or cancel outpatient appointments at any time, with each freed slot being offered to the waiting list before the appointment day. It covers outpatient appointment management but excludes clinical records and prescriptions. Key assumptions include that most patients have mobile phones or email for reminders. Important unresolved architectural decisions relate to handling patient data in compliance with health data regulations, privacy in reminders, the target for the online booking go-live date, and balancing performance against transaction integrity.
